look_here_first: Tiny feathery twice-compound leaves, but NO hooked prickles or straight nodal spines on the local prairie acacia. Cream/white small globose flower heads, low herbaceous/subshrub habit; often rhizomatous. FIRST CHECK FOR NO ARMATURE; THEN COMPARE HEAD COLOR and leaf arrangement.

shared_traits: Herbaceous to subshrubby mimosoid with bipinnate leaves and cream round flower heads.
Unlike the thorny Vachellia and catclaw Senegalia commonly seen, the local taxon is spineless.
Can be rhizomatous and frost dieback, and shoots may respond to touch.
Photo of rhizome/leaf bases and flower head resolves confusion better than habit alone.
priority: absence of paired straight spines and catclaw prickles along mature stem
bipinnate leaf: count pinnae and secondary leaflets
mature flat pod; exact variety concept check
study_strategy.warning: The Master Pool says Acaciella angustissima var. hirta. Kew treats that name as a synonym of Acaciella angustissima var. texensis. Keep both searchable names, one concept. The species-level Acaciella angustissima label in many US floras may not indicate variety.

quick_key.if: spineless low rhizomatous plant, very fine bipinnate leaves, white/cream globose flower heads
quick_key.then: Acaciella angustissima var. texensis (syn. var. hirta)

quick_key.if: paired straight thorn tips next to nodes, spherical GOLD heads
curved catclaw prickles, white spherical heads
touch-responsive leaflets and rosy/pink flower heads
quick_key.then: Mimosa spp.; check habit, prickles and pods

visual_comparison.title: Prairie acacia is usually the thornless one
visual_comparison.memory_rule: WHITE ROUND HEAD + FERNLIKE LEAVES + NO SPINES = check Acaciella.
